hero.title: An infinite canvas runtime for AI‑generated web artifacts.
hero.lede: Keeping hundreds of generated pages alive as iframes doesn't scale. Flattening them to images loses selection and events. Deckle keeps the space in between: cached paint you can still reach into.
hero.eq.aria: Artifact equals source plus durable state plus interaction tree plus paint cache plus optional live runtime
lifecycle.title: Resources follow the viewport, not the document count
lifecycle.lede: Every artifact moves through an explicit state machine. Live DOM, runtimes, and GPU textures are budgeted resources granted by visibility and interaction — never ambient.
lifecycle.aria: cold to parsed to snapshot, snapshot to and from live, live to hibernated, any state to failed
lifecycle.fact1.title: Transitions are transactions.
lifecycle.fact1.body: Allocation happens before publication; a fault leaves the previous committed scene usable.
lifecycle.fact2.title: Snapshots stay selectable.
lifecycle.fact2.body: A texture is one revision of paint output — the interaction tree keeps internal hit testing alive without live DOM.
lifecycle.fact3.title: Stale runtimes can't write.
lifecycle.fact3.body: Revision and epoch checks reject late messages from replaced runtimes before they touch the store.
streaming.title: Built for content that is still being written
streaming.lede: An agent emits an artifact token by token. Every kind commits at its own boundary — a grapheme, a line, a closed markdown construct, a JSON value, a decided HTML tag — and that boundary only ever moves forward, so a reader never sees an interpretation get retracted.
streaming.aria: Per kind, the reason the tail is withheld: text surrogate, code partial line, markdown open fence, json incomplete value, html rawtext script
streaming.fact1.title: Nothing half-parsed reaches the screen.
streaming.fact1.body: A partial tag, an unterminated raw-text element, or an open code fence stays outside the boundary until the stream proves what it is.
streaming.fact2.title: Provisional paint is not authoritative.
streaming.fact2.body: A streaming artifact is pinned against eviction, shows provisional frames, and commits exactly one source revision when it finishes.
streaming.fact3.title: The scene streams too.
streaming.fact3.body: Frames appear and join the spatial index while their content is still arriving, so hit testing and visibility sets work mid-generation.
streaming.fact4.title: Every kind has three presentations.
streaming.fact4.body: Content, loading, and failed. An artifact is loading until its first character commits, media is atomic and only ever loads or fails, and a failure shows its reason beside the code you would quote in a bug report.
packages.title: Backend-independent contracts, tested against oracles
packages.lede: Optimized implementations ship next to naive reference implementations and are differentially tested against them — the oracle stays available as a rollback path.
packages.core: camera, scene store transactions, lifecycle, visibility, budgets
packages.spatial: grid spatial index plus the naive differential oracle
packages.security: static-profile sanitizer, URL policy, quotas, capabilities
packages.runtime: runtime message protocol, epochs, capability-guarded bridge
packages.renderer: retained pictures, canvas-native content rendering, LOD, texture budget
packages.editor: internal hit testing, selection model, virtual event paths
status.title: Honest scope
status.lede: The engine contracts are implemented and tested. The browser-evidence gates are not exited: support for the experimental HTML-in-Canvas APIs is a capability we detect, not a claim we make. No open-source license has been selected yet.
